name: Listen Labs
summary: Listen Labs provides an AI-first customer-research platform, using conversational interviews to speed up insight gathering. It raised a $69 million Series B in January 2026; its valuation was reported above $500 million.
overview: Listen Labs runs AI-assisted customer interviews and research workflows for enterprise teams. The platform is positioned as a faster alternative to conventional qualitative research and has access to a large pool of pre-qualified participants.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: The Series B was led by Ribbit Capital; later Series C discussions did not close.

bull_case: If AI interviews become trusted within product, brand and insight teams, Listen can replace slow research workflows and compound through enterprise usage.
bear_case: Research quality, participant integrity and customer trust are core constraints; the Series B valuation was reported rather than disclosed by the company.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: AI-first customer-research platform built around conversational interviews with real participants.
company: Listen Labs provides an AI-first customer research platform whose interviewer conducts conversational research with recruited participants. It is used for work such as product concepts, messaging and usability testing.

The company announced a $69 million Series B led by Ribbit Capital in January 2026. Listen said it had reached eight-figure annualised revenue, interviewed more than one million people and served hundreds of enterprises; the valuation above $500 million was reported separately.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Listen Labs is a test of whether AI can make qualitative research faster without eroding decision quality. Its competitive edge depends on research rigor, participant access and enterprise trust.

changed.text: Profile reviewed against available public information.

takeaways: Listen uses AI-led interviews for research workflows including product concepts, messaging and usability testing.
Its $69M Series B was company-announced; the $500M-plus valuation is reported context and not a company-disclosed figure.
Panel quality, research rigor and repeat enterprise use matter more than interview volume alone.
